title: Payment Protection Cancellation and Fee Refund Terms
content:
The borrower may cancel a Payment Protection plan at any time; cancelling is the borrower's own decision and is never done for them.

## Terms

1. **Cancellation in the free-look period.** A cancellation during the free-look period refunds every fee charged on the plan only when the current date is no later than the enrollment date plus the free-look days. The free-look period is counted in calendar days starting the day after the enrollment date, and a cancellation on the last day is in time.
2. **Later cancellation.** A later cancellation refunds only the unearned part of the current coverage month's fee, pro rata by the days left in that month (the days after the cancellation date divided by the days in the coverage month), as one refund line against that month's fee.
3. **Termination for another reason.** When coverage terminates for another reason the same pro rata refund applies, and every fee charged for a coverage month starting after a date of death is refunded in full.
4. **Fee charged in error.** A fee charged in error is refunded in full, with the refund reason billing error.
5. **One refund per fee.** Each fee is refunded at most once.
6. **Method of refund.** Refunds are credited back the way the fee was collected.
7. **No re-enrollment.** A cancelled plan cannot be re-enrolled.

A cancellation during the free-look period moves the plan from enrolled to cancelled; a cancellation after it moves the plan from active to cancelled. Each refund is recorded as its own line naming the fee it refunds, the refund date, the amount and the reason, and it reduces the plan's protection fee balance.

## How the conditions are evidenced

- The free-look test reads the enrollment date on the company's record of the plan being cancelled and compares it with the current date.
- The one-refund test reads the plan's refund lines: a fee that already has a refund line naming it is not refunded again.

## The free-look period at its boundary

Call the enrollment date day E. Day 1 of the free-look period is the day after day E, so its last day is day E plus the plan's free-look days.

| Date of cancellation | Refund on cancellation |
|---|---|
| Any day up to and including the last day of the free-look period | every fee charged on the plan |
| Any day after the last day of the free-look period | the unearned part of the current coverage month's fee only, pro rata by the days left in that month |

## Hypothetical pro rata refund

The figures are invented for illustration. A plan's fee for the current coverage month is USD 30.00 and the coverage month has 30 days. The borrower cancels after the free-look period, on a date that leaves 12 days in the coverage month after the cancellation date. The refund is USD 30.00 multiplied by 12 and divided by 30, which is USD 12.00, booked as one refund line against that month's fee. Fees for earlier coverage months are not refunded on this cancellation.
